note: The standard multimodal survey, covering architecture, training strategy, hallucination and evaluation.
title: A survey on multimodal large language models

reading.body:
Multimodal large language models combine text processing with image understanding and other input types, rapidly closing the gap with leading proprietary systems while facing persistent challenges like hallucination that currently limit deployment.

The survey documents how these systems work, how they are trained, and where they fail. It covers architectural choices for connecting different input types to a language model foundation, training strategies that leverage existing text models, and evaluation methods still being developed. The core insight is that multimodal capability is being added to language models incrementally rather than built from scratch, making it accessible to more research groups and organizations.

For AI infrastructure, this matters because multimodal systems require the same computational resources as their text-only predecessors, plus additional training data and engineering to handle images and other modalities. The hallucination problem and evaluation gaps the survey identifies are not primarily compute problems. They are architectural and methodological problems that faster chips alone cannot solve. Organizations planning AI infrastructure should recognize that capability is advancing rapidly across both academic and commercial research, but deployment readiness depends on solving these quality and safety challenges.

The survey does not cover which specific systems are most power-efficient to run, how much additional infrastructure multimodal capabilities actually demand compared to text-only models, or whether the data required for training represents a distinct constraint on scaling.

explain_beginner: Researchers surveyed a new type of artificial intelligence called multimodal large language models, which combine powerful text-processing AI with the ability to understand images and other information types. These systems can perform impressive tasks like writing stories about pictures or solving math problems from images. The survey maps out how these systems work, how they're built and trained, and what problems they still face, suggesting they might be a stepping stone toward more general artificial intelligence.
explain_business: Multimodal large language models represent a significant shift in AI capabilities, enabling systems to process images, text, and other inputs simultaneously with human-level reasoning. Organizations should understand that these models are rapidly advancing and becoming competitive with leading proprietary systems. This survey identifies key technical challenges like hallucination and evaluation gaps that currently limit deployment. Companies evaluating investment in AI infrastructure should track these developments, as capability gaps are closing quickly and architectural approaches are converging across academic and industry efforts.
explain_practitioner: This survey comprehensively reviews multimodal large language models that leverage pretrained language models as their foundation. The authors document architectural designs, training methodologies, dataset approaches, and evaluation frameworks. They catalog emerging capabilities including in-context learning and chain-of-thought reasoning across modalities, and address critical challenges such as hallucination phenomena. The work synthesizes progress toward systems matching GPT-4V performance while identifying extensions across granularity levels, modality types, language support, and deployment scenarios.
